title: If Workgroup Collaboration is a Problem, How Are We Going to Collaborate With the World?
author: Peter S. Kastner
abstract: This Aberdeen Group presentation frames mid-1990s groupware as a rapidly growing market that is about to expand beyond departmental messaging into enterprise, intranet, and internet-enabled collaboration. It mixes market sizing and adoption data with Peter Kastner's guidance on strategy, requirements, best practices, and ROI. The deck also serves as a vendor-facing assessment of Oracle InterOffice as an extensible, server-centric collaboration platform positioned for that transition.
importance_rationale: The deck captures an important inflection point when collaboration shifted from inward-looking groupware toward internet- and intranet-based enterprise coordination, while also documenting Oracle's attempt to shape that market. It is a strong period artifact for market expectations, buyer guidance, and vendor positioning in 1996.
relevance_rationale: Its product specifics are dated, but its strategic advice about enterprise scope, open standards, extensibility, and collaboration across customers and suppliers still maps well to later digital-workplace and SaaS patterns.
prescience_rationale: Kastner was notably right that internet and intranet technologies would become central to collaboration, but the deck overestimated Oracle InterOffice's competitive staying power versus Lotus Notes and Microsoft Exchange. The broader market thesis aged better than the specific vendor call.
